name: Selection Semantics Registry
purpose: Clarify whether δ is treated as a relation, set-valued map, partial function, or selected update rule under restricted conditions.

selection_semantics_classes.definition: δ is treated as a general relation between process states and continuation events.
δ is a map from states to sets of admissible continuation candidates.
δ behaves as a partial function when a specific selection rule (e.g., minimization) is applied.
A refined semantic where δ always returns a single actualization via a mandatory tie-breaking policy.
δ is formally undefined if the admissible image Im_A is empty.

required_policies.definition: Rule for managing multiple equivalent admissible images.
Formal mechanism for selecting a single continuation from a degenerate set.
Governance for cases where no admissible continuation exists (orientation locking).
Limits on the recursive actualization of multiple divergent pathways.
Requirement to record selection failures as structural information.

governance_rules.rule: δ must specify its active semantic class and associated policies.
Selection semantics remain strictly local to the declared CSI neighborhood.

forbidden_claims: Selection semantics prove physical choice or free will.
Tie-breaking policies derive physical selection constants.
Divergent selection justifies the assumption of absolute parallel universes.
